definitions.explanation: Speaking or acting in a straightforward manner without beating around the bush.
Hitting something precisely or correctly, often used when guessing or predicting.

examples.japanese: ずばり{言|い}うと、それは{間違|まちが}いだ。
examples.english: To put it bluntly, that's wrong.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{予想|よそう}がずばり{当|あ}たった。
examples.english: His prediction hit the mark exactly.

examples.japanese: ずばり{核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く{質問|しつもん}だった。
examples.english: It was a question that struck right at the heart of the matter.

notes:
MIMETIC ORIGIN:
Onomatopoeic word suggesting the sound of cutting through something sharply.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・ずばり{言|い}う - to speak bluntly
・ずばり{当|あ}たる - to hit the mark
・ずばり{指摘|してき}する - to point out directly
・ずばり{核心|かくしん}を{突|つ}く - to strike at the heart of the matter

POSITION:
Typically appears before the verb it modifies.

NUANCE:
Conveys directness and precision. When used with {言|い}う, implies the speaker is being frank without softening the message.
